cases.why: the state before this item: thirty Tab stops between the series toggles and the table. Nothing looks different and every mouse interaction still works, which is how it stood unnoticed.

the markup change without the hand-over: every point is tabindex -1, so the chart drops out of the Tab order entirely and a keyboard reader never reaches a single point. Worse than thirty stops, and just as invisible to a mouse.

focus moves but the tabindex does not follow, so after walking to the fifth point, Tab out and Shift+Tab back lands on the first again. The kind of half-roving tabindex that passes a quick manual check, because the arrows themselves still work.

walking every point rather than the visible ones: with Model A switched off, the arrow keys move focus onto points that are display:none, so focus vanishes and the tooltip describes a mark nobody can see.
switching off the series that holds the Tab stop leaves it on a hidden point, and the whole chart drops out of the Tab order until the series is switched back on.

wrapping from the last point to the first reads as a jump across the whole chart with no cue, and a reader holding the arrow key cannot tell where the ends are. The ends stop, as they do in the rest of the page's keyboard handling.
